english.title: Knowingly cause to be administered to an animal an unlicensed substance / product

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Examination for Residues and Maximum Residue Limits

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowingly caused to be administered to an animal, namely **(..SPECIFY ANIMAL..), an unlicensed substance, namely **(..SPECIFY SUBSTANCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 6(2) and 23 of the Animals and Animal Products (Examination for Residues and Maximum Residue Limits) Regulations 1997.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time Limit on Prosecutions
No prosecution shall be begun after the expiry of -

(a) three years from commission of the offence; or
(b) one year from its discovery by the prosecutor,

whichever is the earlier.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
